shots.phrase: Begin by framing Introduction to Raster Graphics Pipeline as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results.
The OpenGL graphics pipeline processes vertices through programmable shader stages.
List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion.
Now define Primitive Assembly and Clipping precisely enough that another learner could test the definition.
Consider this worked case: A polygon with one vertex outside the camera frustum is clipped to intersect the view volume boundaries.
A precise definition makes later examples easier to evaluate and revise.
With the foundation in place, examine how Rasterization and Interpolation operates in a concrete sequence.
Consider this worked case: A triangle is rasterized into a set of pixels, with color and normal values interpolated across each pixel based on barycentric coordinates.
The trace converts an abstract statement into an inspectable sequence.
Next, compare the choices involved in Fragment Processing and Depth Testing and make the decision criteria explicit.
Consider this worked case: A backface-occluded triangle is discarded because its depth value is greater than the stored depth buffer value at that pixel.
Using shared criteria turns a preference into a defensible technical choice.
Apply Blending and Coordinate Spaces to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition.
Coordinate spaces, sampling, and numerical precision must remain explicit.
Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step.
Examine the tradeoffs in Geometric Modeling and Transformations, including what improves and what becomes more difficult.
Consider this worked case: A 3-D model is translated, rotated, and scaled using transformation matrices to position it in the scene.
Making the tradeoff visible prevents a local improvement from hiding a larger cost.
Stress-test the reasoning around Viewing and Projection with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome.
Viewing maps a scene through a camera model to an image.
Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds.
Use Shading and Texture Mapping to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action.
Texture mapping associates image data with geometric surfaces.
Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause.
Connect Hardware Shaders and Rasterization Focus to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system.
The course will focus on rasterization techniques and emphasize the hardware rasterization pipeline including the use of hardware shaders.
Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations.
Finish with Practical Analysis Checklist as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis.
Visual correctness follows from explicit conventions, assumptions, sampling decisions, and measurable error.
For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step.
